Metrocentre needs a service and value conversation. 58 reviews at 4.57 against 62 at 4.73, negatives 6.5 per cent to 12.1 per cent, twice the fleet rate.

Four complaints are price and four are taste, and they land together: one guest paid £72 and described tiny steak, grey noodles and poor karaage on 09/08/2026. Three more are inattentive service, one guest on 10/08/2026 chasing drinks, cutlery, tissues and the bill. On 28/08/2026: "they add a tip to the bill without consent".

Kieran Day owns check back and clearing. Ka Ho and Óisín Patrick Darragh should take the service charge script here first. No staff member was praised by name in August.

quarter|2026-Q3|site|M15.t: Metrocentre doubled its negatives, four to 11, taking the rate to 9.2% from 3.8% on 120 reviews. The split is nine food quality and six service, with four inattentive, three staggered dishes and two slow bill mentions. The worst single visit, on 09/08/2026 at £72, describes noodles as "clearly pre heated grey pre packaged crap" with a tiny steak portion. Three further reviews describe chasing drinks, cutlery and the bill, and even 4 and 5-star reviews flag dishes landing at different times. Kieran Day owns pass sequencing and section cover; Óisín Patrick Darragh should look at the rota. Only two praise mentions here, which is thin.

week|2026-08-24|site|M15.t: Metrocentre came in at 4.48 on 21 reviews, just under the 4.5 line on a sample big enough to mean it, with 3 negatives. Two of the three are about money rather than the meal: a tip added to the bill without consent on 28/08/2026, and a straight price comparison against a competitor. The third, on 24/08/2026, is mediocre food with forgetful service and no regular soy sauce on offer. Trading is strong, sales 21.68 per cent above target on 3,239 covers and efficiency 95 green, so this is a till and script fix, not a performance issue. Kieran Day to brief how the service charge is introduced, and to get standard soy sauce back on the floor.

I visited this restaurant today in a very good mood, expecting a pleasant dining experience, but unfortunately it turned out to be quite disappointing.

When we arrived, there were several larger tables available near the window and around us. However, we were seated at a very small table for two, which felt quite cramped—especially considering the size and number of dishes typically served in Japanese cuisine.

What I found particularly confusing and unfair was that just one minute later, another party of two was seated at one of the larger tables. In fact, other tables around us with the same number of guests were also given more spacious seating. I really don’t understand why we were treated differently.

When I politely asked the staff if we could move to a larger table, we were relocated to a very remote corner where there was hardly any service at all. This made the situation even worse and significantly affected our dining experience.

Overall, this kind of arrangement and handling felt quite inconsiderate and left a negative impression.

We visited this Maki & Ramen location twice, and over both visits, the food was exceptional. The Black Dragon roll and Black Garlic Tonkotsu are standout entries on the menu, and we couldn't recommend the food here enough.

However, on a fairly busy Saturday evening visit, I was left for approx. 30 mins without food while my husband was served his very promptly. In fairness, our waitress did explain that what I had ordered was taking an "extra 15 minutes", but after those 15 minutes had been and gone, and it had actually turned into 30 minutes, all I could do during that time was watch him eat his order by himself before it went cold.... and I just got hungrier.

When my food did eventually arrive, it was as I said exceptional, but now it was a role reversal, and I was the one left eating by myself instead.

The music was also quite loud, and it was impossible to have a normal conversation without shouting at eachother.

On balance I'd definitely recommend this location, but if Saturday's service is anything to go by, don't arrive hungry and ready to eat, because you'll be "hangry" by the time your food gets to you.

Unfortunately, restaurant no longer offers a regular, non-halal Steak Tataki Ramen. Previously customers could choose between halal and non-halal beef but now the website states that all beef used in their ramen is halal, leaving customers with no alternative.

I believe this is unfair to customers who, for personal or religious reasons, do not wish to consume halal meat. As a Christian, I do not believe I should be expected to accept a religiously prepared product when I previously had the option to choose otherwise.

I fully respect the right of Muslim customers to choose halal food. However I believe the same consideration should be given to customers who prefer non-halal meat. Previously both options were available, but now only halal beef is offered meaning that customers who do not want halal meat have lost their choice.

In my opinion, a restaurant should respect the different dietary preferences and beliefs of all its customers rather than remove an option that was previously available.

Unfortunately, this change has left me disappointed. I would like to see Maki&Ramen reintroduce the non-halal beef option for its Steak Tataki Ramen.

One star due to the loss of choice and the lack of consideration for customers who do not wish to eat halal meat.
